chunks: As for what was narrated by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Jibra'il عليه السلام came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله with the times of salat (prayer). He came to him when the sun had declined, and commanded him, so he performed Zuhr; then he came to him when the shadow had increased by one stature, and commanded him, so he performed 'Asr; then he came to him when the sun had set, and commanded him, so he performed Maghrib; then he came to him when the twilight had fallen, and commanded him, so he performed 'Isha'; then he came to him when dawn rose, and commanded him, so he performed Subh. Then he came to him the next day when the shadow had increased by one stature, and commanded him, so he performed Zuhr; then he came to him when the shadow had increased by two statures, and commanded him, so he performed 'Asr; then he came to him when the sun had set, and commanded him, so he performed Maghrib; then he came to him when one-third of the night had passed, and commanded him, so he performed 'Isha'; then he came to him when the morning had brightened, and commanded him, so he performed Subh. Then he said: 'What lies between them is a time.'
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Bashir, from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“Jibra'il عليه السلام came,” and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Abi Khadijah, except that he said, in place of one stature and two statures: “one cubit and two cubits.”
And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Ribat, from Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, who said: Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام said:

“Jibra'il عليه السلام descended upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله,” and he related the hadith like the first one, and mentioned in place of one stature and two statures: “two feet and four feet.”

So it is not for anyone to say that these reports indicate that the beginning of the time and the end are equal, because he said, “What lies between them is a time.” For it is not impossible that what lies between the two times be made a time, even if the first is more excellent than it. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الظِّلُّ: the shadow used to measure time
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: the dawn marking the beginning of Subh prayer time
key_terms.مَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَقْتٌ: the interval between the two endpoints is also a valid time

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Jibra'il عليه السلام teach about the beginning and ending times of the daily salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This report describes Jibra'il عليه السلام teaching the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله the times of the daily salat (prayer), first at their earliest points and then at later points. It establishes that the interval between these limits is also valid prayer time, while indicating that the earlier time is more excellent.
